slots.purpose: A and G: the wordmark (whole, or its first part). From the brand kit name.
A and G: the wordmark's second part, drawn in the accent. Empty for a one-word brand (the mark and the wordmark are already the two counter-bouncing parts).
The brand mark (brand kit logo). Empty = a monogram in the accent.
B: the entry surface's title (sign-in, onboarding or first run).
B: one line under the title.
B: first sign-in option the product really offers. Empty = none.
B: second real sign-in option. Empty = none.
B and C: the divider text above the field.
B and C: the field's label.
B and C: the field's placeholder.
B and C: the surface's button; its press in C ignites the cut.
C: what gets typed into the field. A sample value, never a real person's data.
D: what the one number counts.
D: where the count starts on screen.
D: the number users of the product would quote. Never invented.
D: the short line under the number (a unit or a total).
D: 0–4 real steps of the process behind the number; the first is done, the second is active and ticks done.
E: the product's real primary navigation, 3–5 rows. The first row is the one chosen.
E: one row after a divider (often Settings). Empty = none; then up to 5 main rows fit.
E: one line under the list, arriving with the choice.
F: the page the chosen nav row opens.
F: one line under the page title.
F: the product's real primary create button.
F: a second real button beside it. Empty = none.
F: the heading of what the create button opens.
F: exactly 4 real choices as {name, meta}; the second is chosen. name ≤ 18 chars, meta ≤ 14.
F: what the choice asks for next.
G: at most one closing line. Empty = the lockup alone.
